question.question:
A fictional robo-advisor holds 25 shares of ETF Q bought at 106 USD each and sells them all at 79.25 USD each. 30 days later it buys 20 shares of the same ETF at 117.25 USD each. Wash-sale rule: if the first sale was a loss and the repurchase is within 30 days (inclusive), the per-share loss times the smaller of shares sold and repurchased is disallowed and added to the new lot's total basis; a first-sale gain is unaffected. Later the same tax year the whole new lot is sold at 64.75 USD each with no further repurchase; nothing else is realized. The net result is the allowed signed first-sale result plus the signed second-sale result. If the net is a loss, at most 1200 USD is deductible this year and the excess carries forward; if a gain, deduction and carryforward are zero. What loss in USD carries forward?

Answer format: return only the exact numeric value interpreted in `usd`, using finite-decimal notation when it terminates in base 10 and an irreducible `numerator/denominator` fraction otherwise, with no unit label or additional text.

slots.description: Loss on the first sale disallowed by the wash-sale rule, USD
Total cost basis of the repurchased lot after adding disallowed loss, USD
Signed net realized result for the year, positive means gain, USD
Net loss deductible this year after the annual cap, USD
